newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Only three Moslems go to Srebrenica to vote.
newsitem.headline: Only three Moslems go to Srebrenica to vote.

text.p: Only three Moslem refugees from the former eastern Bosnian enclave of Srebrenica showed up on Saturday morning to be taken back to vote, though around 8,000 refugees had been expected.
Buses were ready in Kladanj to take thousands of Moslems across the ethnic boundary line from the Moslem-Croat Federation into the Bosnian Serb Republic, a Reuter reporter at the scene said.

The Srebrenica refugees, most of whom fled when the enclave was overrun by Serb forces in July last year, were supposed to vote in the village of Podravanje, 20 km (12 miles) from Srebrenica, described by them as a village held by hardline nationalist Serbs or chetniks.
Up to 8,000 Srebrenica men are still missing and many are feared to have been killed in Serb ambushes while trying to reach Bosnian government territory.

Husein Efendic, 45, from Srebrenica told Reuters: "If I feared to vote there I would not have come but it is a shame that people did not come. I expected all of us to come and go there because the elections are supposed to bring us a better future."

Municipal elections in the Bosnian Serb Republic were cancelled because of irregularities in voter registration. Many Moslem refugees will vote in their new homes in the Moslem-Croat Federation for a president, parliament and cantonal assemblies, instead of travelling back to former homes which are now in Serb hands.
On Friday, the leader of the Srebrenica women's association in Tuzla told Reuters the voting arrangements in Podravanje were a humiliation.
"They are doing this so the world thinks there is freedom of movement in Bosnia but they send us to a chetnik stronghold," Fatima Husejnovic said.

Meho Avdagic, 52, said: "There are not even eight of us to fill up a single bus. This is a big, big shame. However, whether these elections are true or not I will one day go back to Srebrenica. I could live with Serbs again and I don't care what they think about it."

War crimes investigators on Thursday found piles of human bones, skulls and clothes buried at a farm in northeast Bosnia. They believe the mass grave will provide evidence of a massacre of Srebrenica Moslems.

Reports from correspondents across Bosnia on Saturday suggested few refugees had so far crossed ethnic boundary lines to vote. Thousands of Serb refugees have crossed from Belgrade into the Bosnian Serb Republic.
